- When sentiment is high (≥0.7) and forecast is significantly below recent history, adjust upward by 1–3% to reflect bullish momentum.  
- When sentiment is low (≤0.3) and forecast is above recent history, reduce forecast by 1–3% to avoid overreaction.  
- If forecast shows a sharp spike followed by a steep drop, reduce the immediate post-spike values by 5–10% to account for volatility decay.  
- For 30-day forecasts, if the last 3–5 days of history show strong mean reversion (e.g., 2–3 consecutive drops), apply a downward bias of 2–5% to the forecast tail.  
- If sentiment history shows a recent reversal (e.g., from high to low), adjust forecast to align with the new sentiment trend, especially in the first 7–10 days of the forecast horizon.  
- Avoid forecasting below 60% of the 18-day moving average unless sentiment is strongly bearish (≤0.2) and recent price action confirms a breakout.
